For selected and reference radii r_s and r_r, D_s=2r_s and D_r=2r_r. The geometric multiplier is M_D=D_s/D_r=r_s/r_r; the selected tube is larger than the reference tube.

With thermodynamic reaction enthalpies ΔH_1 and ΔH_2 and molar volumetric rates r_1 and r_2, q_rxn=(-ΔH_1)r_1+(-ΔH_2)r_2. Both reactions are exothermic, so each forward reaction contributes positive heat generation. Rate and volume units must be consistent.

The wall heat flux is q_wall=U(T_wall-T_c), where U is the overall heat-transfer coefficient and T_c is coolant temperature. Tube-size transfer requires compatible reaction heat, transport, fluid properties and thermal boundary conditions.

M_D=D_s/D_r, M_Q=Q_s/Q_r and M_P=P_s/P_r. At equal mean velocity, M_Q=M_D². For equal feed composition, M_P=M_Q(Y_s/Y_r); the simulated production multiplier is 126.455258. Yield changes explain why production need not follow geometry alone.

For N identical independent tubes, P_total=N P_tube. This ideal capacity estimate assumes uniform distribution and matching per-tube conditions; integrated operation, control and reliability have not been demonstrated.

For a cylindrical tube, A_wall/V=2/r=4/D. Hence (A/V)_s/(A/V)_r=r_r/r_s. Enlargement reduces wall area available for heat removal per unit volume and requires assessment of local heat generation and heat transfer.

Liquid volumetric flow Q is a whole-stream volume rate; net TBHP production is a species mass rate. P_net=M_TBHP(Q_out C_out-Q_in C_in). The simulated selected-tube net TBHP production is 0.402372685 g/min.

The cooling boundary is q_wall=U(T_wall-T_c). Changing U or T_c changes heat removal and the coupled temperature field, so the original screening result cannot automatically be carried over. The altered case requires re-evaluation.

D=2r defines the relation between diameter and radius. M_D=D_s/D_r describes geometric enlargement. N is a separate parallel-tube count, giving P_total=N P_tube under ideal identical operation; it does not change a tube’s local geometry.
